originality.broader_coverage: Standard singular-value lower bounds plus Weyl perturbation give a uniform (-0.7,0.7) gap on the same full box.
checked_sources: Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press, 2013 (singular-value and Hermitian eigenvalue perturbation inequalities)
originality.claim_vs_prior_implication: The standard estimate strictly dominates the stated 0.6 theorem, so the final scientific claim is covered even if the Riccati certificate is independently valid.
originality.equivalent_formulations: Recast the Jacobi matrix as a bipartite block matrix plus a diagonal perturbation.
originality.exact_database_or_table: Not needed for the decisive comparison; the claim is mechanically implied by general textbook inequalities.
originality.rationale: A stronger result follows immediately from standard singular-value and Hermitian perturbation inequalities. After odd/even permutation, the zero-diagonal part is [[0,B],[B^T,0]] with B=S+W, where S is diagonal with entries at least 1.4 and W is a weighted one-step shift of operator norm at most 0.6. Hence sigma_min(B) >= 1.4-0.6 = 0.8. The diagonal disorder has operator norm at most 0.1, so Weyl's inequality leaves five eigenvalues at most -0.7 and five at least +0.7. Therefore the whole claimed (-0.6,0.6) gap, including the 5/5 split, is a direct corollary of a stronger textbook estimate.

final_claim: Every 10×10 Jacobi matrix in the stated dimer disorder box has no eigenvalue in (-0.6,0.6), with five eigenvalues below -0.6 and five above 0.6; the Riccati/Sturm certificate improves the listed Gershgorin/Brauer baselines.
